boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Haverford study settings, from heritage reading rooms to reservable collaboration spaces, with current access and room-use details.

cards.entity_name: Nan and Bill Harris Digital Scholarship Commons
cards.title: Spread Out in the Digital Commons
cards.subtitle: Flexible, technology-rich study on Lutnick Library’s second level
cards.notes: Bring a collaborative or digital project; use the flexible seating, Google Jamboards, and nearby technology-rich group rooms.
cards.short_summary: A flexible workspace designed for technology-assisted scholarship and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford identifies this level-two Lutnick space as featuring flexible seating, Google Jamboards, and technology-rich group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located on level 2 of Lutnick Library; consult the current library-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Put the Full Team Around One Table
cards.subtitle: A 14-seat group room with presentation and conferencing equipment
cards.notes: Reserve this room for a large working session, then connect to the 85-inch display or integrated web-conferencing system.
cards.short_summary: The largest documented Lutnick group-study room supports presentations and remote participants.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 202 has a 14-seat rectangular table, an 85-inch display, a Mersive POD, professional audio, Listen Assist, and a PTZ webcam.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; access is subject to Lutnick Library hours.

cards.title: Workshop a Draft in Room 129
cards.subtitle: A medium group room for six, with capacity for two more
cards.notes: Book Room 129 for a discussion or rehearsal; its table box, webcam, display, and Listen Assist support shared work.
cards.short_summary: A reservable medium room sized for a seminar-style study session.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford describes Room 129 as a medium group-study room with a rectangular table, six chairs, a 65-inch display, webcam, Mersive POD, and Listen Assist.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; the stated configuration seats six and can accommodate two more.

cards.title: Gather Four Around the Round Table
cards.subtitle: A compact group room with a 55-inch display
cards.notes: Reserve Room 126 for a four-person problem set or edit session, and use the display wallplate and Mersive POD to share work.
cards.short_summary: A compact reservable room with an equal-footing round-table layout.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 126 is one of Lutnick’s approximately 13-by-10-foot small group rooms, furnished with a round table, four chairs, a 55-inch display, wallplate, and Mersive POD.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; access is subject to Lutnick Library hours.

cards.title: Map the Problem on a Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: A ten-seat science-library collaboration room
cards.notes: Reserve Room 305B when the work needs diagrams or shared calculations; the whiteboard and large monitor suit visible thinking.
cards.short_summary: A medium group room pairing ten seats with analog and digital work surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists White Science Library Room 305B as a medium group-study room with a whiteboard, large flat-screen monitor, and seating for ten.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; White Science Library is on the third floor of KINSC-Hilles.

cards.title: Take a Four-Person Science Huddle
cards.subtitle: A small room with a board for working through ideas
cards.notes: Choose Room 304C for a focused four-person session; reserve ahead and use the room’s board to keep calculations visible.
cards.short_summary: A small reservable science-library room built around face-to-face work.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford lists White Science Library Room 304C among its four-seat small group rooms, equipped with a whiteboard or chalkboard.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through the College room-reservation system; White Science Library is on the third floor of KINSC-Hilles.

cards.title: Reserve Two Hours of Solo Focus
cards.subtitle: Individual carrels with a clear reservation priority
cards.notes: Claim a two-hour block through EMS or a nearby kiosk; without a booking, use an open carrel but yield to its reservation holder.
cards.short_summary: A structured solo-work option with short bookings and semester access for thesis writers.
cards.evidence_claim: Lutnick carrels can be reserved for two-hour blocks, while another block is available to thesis writers for semester-long reservations.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through EMS or the carrel-area kiosk. Unreserved use is allowed, but occupants must yield to reservation holders.

cards.title: Read Beneath the Vaulted Ceiling
cards.subtitle: A heritage reading environment inside Lutnick Library
cards.notes: Settle into the Philips Wing for reading-oriented work, and consult the building map first to distinguish its tiers and entrances.
cards.short_summary: A named historic wing offering a visually distinctive library setting.
cards.evidence_claim: The Libraries’ Places & Hours page identifies the Philips Wing with a photograph of its vaulted ceilings, and the official building map labels the wing across multiple tiers.
cards.access_notes: Inside Lutnick Library and available subject to current building hours; no separate reservation rule is stated on the source page.

cards.title: Find the Rufus Jones Study
cards.subtitle: A named heritage room in Lutnick Library’s Philips Wing
cards.notes: Use the official floor map to locate this tucked-away named room, then confirm availability on arrival because no booking policy is posted.
cards.short_summary: A map-documented heritage room within the older portion of Lutnick Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford’s official Lutnick Library floor map labels the Rufus Jones Study within the Philips Wing.
cards.source_title: Haverford College Magill Library Floor Maps
cards.access_notes: Located inside Lutnick Library. The official map confirms the room, but the College does not publish a separate reservation rule for it.

cards.title: Work Directly with the Archives
cards.subtitle: A supervised research room for collection-based study
cards.notes: Bring a laptop, tablet, phone, camera, pencil, or paper; register daily, store other belongings in a locker, and keep food and water outside.
cards.short_summary: A public research setting reserved for hands-on work with special-collections materials.
cards.evidence_claim: The Reading Room welcomes researchers without an affiliation or ID requirement, but is reserved for people using Quaker & Special Collections materials under posted handling rules.
cards.source_title: Accessing Materials & Reproductions | Haverford College Libraries
cards.access_notes: Appointments are not required. Register and sign in each day; the room is only for researchers using collection materials.
